courses.title: AI Influencer Course
courses.description:
## AI Influencer Mastery

Learn how to **create, grow, and monetize your own AI influencer** from scratch with a practical, step-by-step system.

Across **34 focused lessons**, you’ll learn how to build a consistent AI character, generate realistic photos and videos, create talking and lip-sync content, edit professional Reels, and develop a strong social media presence.

You’ll also explore real-world applications including **AI product photography, fashion try-ons, UGC videos, brand collaborations, client outreach, pricing, portfolio building, affiliate marketing, and digital products**.

Designed for beginners, creators, freelancers, and business owners, the course focuses on practical execution without requiring coding, professional cameras, or advanced editing skills.

**By the end, you’ll have a complete AI creator system—from your first character to content, clients, and monetization opportunities.**

videos.title: Introduction
videos.description:
## Lesson 1 — Introduction

### What is an AI Influencer?

An AI Influencer is a **digital creator or virtual model** that can create photos, videos, and social media content without requiring a camera setup, physical model, or expensive production.

With just a phone and the right AI tools, you can build a complete **content + business system**.

### What Can an AI Influencer Do?

* **Content Creation** — Create reels, photos, and regular content for Instagram and YouTube.
* **Business Content** — Produce professional product photos, videos, and promotional creatives for brands.
* **Monetization** — Explore opportunities through sponsorships, brand deals, affiliate marketing, and digital products.

### Why Is This Possible Now?

Modern AI tools have made content creation faster, easier, and more accessible. You do not need coding skills, professional editing knowledge, or expensive equipment to get started.

### Common Mistake

Many beginners assume AI content creation is too technical. In reality, once you understand the right workflow, the process becomes simple and repeatable.

### Today’s Task

Decide your primary goal:

**Create content, work with brands, or monetize your AI skills.**

This course will guide you through all three paths step by step.

*Concept Lesson — no generation prompt is required in this lesson.*

## Lesson 2 — Tools Setup

### You Only Need 3 Tools

All three tools work on your phone, and you can start for free.

* **Google Flow** — The main tool used in this course for generating AI photos and videos.
* **VN** — A free video editing app for cuts, captions, music, and final reel editing.
* **ChatGPT** — Used for scripts, dialogues, prompt ideas, and content planning.

### Important Setup Rules

* Use the **same Google account** across your AI tools wherever possible. This keeps your work, files, and history easier to manage.
* Free plans may have daily generation limits, but they are enough for learning and practice.
* Avoid paying for premium tools at the beginning. Upgrade only when your work actually requires it.
* Create a folder on your phone called **“AI Studio”** and keep all three tools together for quick access.

### Common Mistake

Using multiple accounts and later losing track of files, projects, or previous work.

### Today’s Task

Set up all three tools, use one primary Google account, and create your **AI Studio** folder.

*Concept Lesson — no generation prompt is required in this lesson.*

videos.title: Creating Your AI Influencer Character
videos.description:
## Lesson 3 — Creating Your AI Influencer Character

### The Most Important Concept: Consistency

Your AI influencer should have the **same recognizable face across every photo and video**. Consistency helps the character feel believable and builds trust with both audiences and brands.

### Define Your Character

Before generating the face, decide the basic identity of your influencer and save it somewhere.

Include:

* **Name**
* **Age**
* **City**
* **Personality**
* **Interests**

For example: **Neha, 22, Mumbai, confident and friendly, interested in fashion and travel.**

These details will shape the style and personality of your future content.

### Create the Reference Photo

Generate the character using a detailed face prompt and create a few variations.

Choose the most natural and realistic result, then save it as your **Reference Photo**.

This reference image will be used throughout the course for different poses, outfits, locations, product shoots, and videos.

### Common Mistake

Creating a new face every time you generate content. This breaks character consistency and makes the influencer look different across posts.

**Always work from the same original reference photo.**

### Today’s Task

Write down your character details, generate a few face options, choose the best one, and save it as your **Reference Photo**.

videos.title: Learning to Write Prompts Why Prompting Matters
videos.description:
## Lesson 4 — Learning to Write Prompts

### Why Prompting Matters

Prompt writing is one of the most important skills in this course.

A strong prompt gives you a strong result. A weak prompt leads to poor and inconsistent output.

### The 5 Parts of a Good Prompt

1. **Who** — Define the subject clearly, such as age, gender, and nationality.
   *Example: a young Indian woman in her early 20s*

2. **Face Details** — Describe important facial features.
   *Example: oval face, brown eyes, wavy hair, natural smile*

3. **Outfit** — Mention the clothing clearly and specifically.
   *Example: white cotton kurti*

4. **Location / Background** — Add the setting and mood.
   *Example: sitting in a café with soft window light*

5. **Style** — Explain how the final image should look.
   *Example: realistic, candid, shot on iPhone*

### Prompting Rules

* Write prompts in **English** for better results.
* If needed, use ChatGPT to translate your idea into a proper English prompt.
* Avoid vague words like **“beautiful”** or **“gorgeous.”**
* Focus on **clear visual details** instead.
* Keep the prompt simple and specific. Asking for too many things at once can confuse the AI.

### Common Mistake

Using vague prompts like *“create a beautiful girl”*, which usually produces random and inconsistent results.

### Today’s Task

Write **5 prompts** for your AI influencer.

Keep the base character the same, and only change the **outfit** and **location** in each prompt.

videos.title: Maintaining the Same Face Across Different Poses
videos.description:
## Lesson 5 — Maintaining the Same Face Across Different Poses

### Core Concept

The goal of this lesson is to keep your AI influencer’s identity visually consistent while changing the pose, outfit, angle, or location.

To do this, use your saved **reference photo** along with a clear instruction such as:

**“Use this exact face. Same woman, same facial features.”**

This helps the AI preserve the same identity while generating new variations of the character.

### Important Guidelines

* Always generate new images from the **original reference photo**.
* Do **not** use a newly generated image as the next reference.
* Reusing generated outputs as new references can gradually change the face over time.
* AI may not produce a perfect match every time, so it is best to generate multiple options and select the strongest one.

### Best Practice

For each idea, generate **4 variations** and keep the **best 1** that most closely matches your original character.

### Common Mistake

A common mistake is continuing the process with a newly generated image instead of the original reference. This creates **character drift**, where the face slowly changes and loses consistency.

### Today’s Task

Use your original reference photo to create **5 different images** of the same character with different **poses, outfits, and locations**.

Save the best results for future lessons and content creation.

Detailed Notes
A critical rule is to return to the original reference every time. The course compares repeated re-referencing
to a copy-of-a-copy problem: if each newly generated image becomes the next reference, small facial

and keeping the strongest one. The workflow is therefore controlled selection rather than expecting a
single generation to be perfect.
Useful pose changes include standing, sitting, walking and changing the camera angle. The professional
principle is to vary composition while keeping identity stable. This gives the feed visual variety without
making the character look like different people.

videos.title: Creating Different Outfit Styles
videos.description:
## Lesson 6 — Creating Different Outfit Styles

### Build a Versatile Wardrobe

A strong AI influencer should be able to appear in different styles depending on the content, audience, or brand requirement.

Create a wardrobe across four key categories:

* **Casual** — Ideal for everyday, relatable content.
* **Ethnic** — Suitable for Indian fashion, festivals, and traditional campaigns.
* **Western** — Works well for modern, premium, and professional looks.
* **Party Wear** — Best for events, celebrations, and occasion-based content.

### Important Guidelines

* Match the **lighting** to the outfit and mood.
  For example, use natural daylight for casual looks and warmer evening lighting for party wear.
* Keep each prompt focused.
* A good structure is: **main outfit + one accessory + suitable lighting**.
* Avoid adding too many clothing details or accessories in a single prompt, as this can reduce accuracy.

### Common Mistake

Creating content in only one style limits the variety of your portfolio and reduces the range of brands you can work with.

### Today’s Task

Create **4 images** of your AI influencer — one each in **Casual, Ethnic, Western, and Party Wear**.

Save the strongest result from each style for future content and brand work.

videos.title: Creating Different Locations
videos.description:
## Lesson 7 — Creating Different Locations

### Create Variety Through Locations

Changing locations helps your AI influencer feel more realistic, versatile, and suitable for different types of content.

Focus on five useful location categories:

* **Home** — Relatable and natural everyday content.
* **Café** — Aesthetic lifestyle and social media content.
* **Street** — Ideal for fashion and candid urban shots.
* **Nature** — Suitable for travel, outdoor, and lifestyle content.
* **Premium** — Hotels, rooftops, lounges, or luxury-inspired settings for high-end brand visuals.

### Important Guidelines

* Do not describe only the location — describe the **atmosphere** as well.
  For example: *“sunset in the background, soft breeze, hair moving naturally.”*
* Match the **pose** to the environment. Candid actions usually look more natural than stiff standing poses.
* Avoid relying on famous landmarks, as AI may recreate them inaccurately.
* Use broader descriptions such as **“historic Indian architecture”** or **“luxury hotel rooftop”** for more reliable results.

### Common Mistake

Using the same standing pose in every location. This makes the content repetitive and can make the character look artificial.

### Today’s Task

Create **5 images** of your AI influencer — one in each location category:

**Home, Café, Street, Nature, and Premium.**

Choose the strongest result from each category and save them for your content library.

videos.title: Making AI Images Look More Realistic Remove the Artificial AI Look
videos.description:
## Lesson 8 — Making AI Images Look More Realistic

### Remove the Artificial AI Look

One of the most important skills in AI content creation is making your images look natural rather than overly polished or artificial.

To reduce the typical “AI look,” include these four details in your prompt:

1. **Natural skin texture, visible pores**
2. **Slight imperfections, a few flyaway hairs**
3. **Shot on iPhone or DSLR**
4. **Soft natural light**

You should also add the word **“candid”** to encourage more natural poses and a realistic, casual photo feel.

### Important Guidelines

* Focus on subtle realism instead of perfection.
* Small imperfections often make the image feel more human and believable.
* Camera-based phrasing such as **“shot on iPhone”** or **“shot on DSLR”** helps create a more authentic photographic style.
* Natural lighting usually produces softer and more convincing results than overly dramatic or artificial lighting.

### Words to Avoid

Avoid terms such as:

* **Ultra realistic**
* **8K**
* **HD**
* **Perfect**

These words often make the image look more artificial, overly smooth, or visually exaggerated.

### Common Mistake

A common mistake is assuming that phrases like **“8K ultra realistic”** will automatically produce a realistic image. In many cases, they do the opposite and make the result look more artificial.

### Today’s Task

Take **3 older images** of your AI influencer and regenerate them using these realism details.

Then compare the old and new versions **side by side** to see how much more natural the updated images look.

videos.title: Fixing AI Photo Quality
videos.description:
## Lesson 9 — Fixing AI Photo Quality

### Quality Check Before Saving

Before saving any AI-generated image, review these four areas carefully:

1. **Hands and Fingers** — Check that the hands look natural and the fingers are correctly formed.
2. **Eyes** — Make sure both eyes are aligned and looking in the same direction.
3. **Background** — Look for distorted, melted, or unrealistic objects.
4. **Face Consistency** — Compare the face with your original reference photo.

Only save images that pass this basic quality check.

### How to Repair an Image

If only one part of the image is incorrect, use a targeted instruction such as:

**“Fix only the hands. Keep the face, outfit, pose, and background exactly the same.”**

The word **“only”** is important because it tells the AI to change just one specific area.

You can also:

* **Crop** the problematic part if it is near the edge of the image.
* Change the pose so difficult areas are less visible, such as **hands in pockets, holding a bag, or arms crossed**.

### Important Rule

Use a maximum of **one repair attempt per image**.

If an image has multiple problems, it is usually better to generate a new one instead of repeatedly editing the same image.

### Common Mistake

Trying to fix the same image again and again. Multiple edits can reduce quality and may also change the character’s face or other important details.

### Today’s Task

Review all the images you have created so far using the four-point checklist.

Keep the strong images, repair those with a single minor issue, and regenerate any image with multiple problems.
videos.notes:
AI INFLUENCER COURSE
LESSON 09 · PHOTO QUALITY    FIX
Module: Photo Skills    |    Study Notes Edition
Learning Objective
Before saving or delivering an image, the course recommends a four-point inspection: hands/fingers, eyes,
background, and face match. These checks are important because an image can look attractive overall
while containing one obvious AI artifact.
Detailed Notes
For repairs, the source recommends making a narrowly targeted instruction such as fixing only the hand
while preserving the face, hairstyle, outfit, pose, lighting and background. Cropping or changing the pose to
hide a problematic hand is another option.
The strongest workflow is selective. The course recommends a maximum of one repair on a photo. If
multiple things are wrong, repeatedly editing the same image can degrade it further, so regenerating a
cleaner image may be better.
A professional quality-control checklist should be completed before every export. Do not judge only the
face: inspect hands, eyes, objects, edges, background and identity consistency. The final image should be
treated as a deliverable, not merely as a generation result.
What to Remember
• Keep the workflow repeatable and organized.
• Follow the course’s stated process before adding complexity.

## Lesson 10 — Building a 30-Photo Content Bank

### Create Content in Batches

Instead of creating content every day, build an entire month’s content in advance.

A simple structure is:

**30 Photos = 5 Outfits × 6 Locations**

Batch creation helps you stay consistent, save time, and avoid the pressure of generating something new every day.

### How to Build Your Content Bank

Use ChatGPT to create **30 numbered photo prompts** based on your character, outfits, locations, lighting, and realism guidelines.

Then generate each prompt in Google Flow using your **original reference photo**.

This gives you a structured content library that you can use throughout the month.

### Keep the Feed Natural

Not every generated image will be perfect, and that is normal.

From 30 generations, keep only the strongest results that match your character and quality standards.

To make your content feel more authentic, include at least **one candid-style image for every five photos**.

### Common Mistake

Creating one image every day from scratch.

This quickly becomes repetitive and difficult to maintain. **Batch creation is a more efficient and consistent workflow.**

### Today’s Task

Create a list of **30 numbered prompts** and generate at least **10 photos today**.

Complete the remaining images over the next two days and save only the best results in your content bank.

videos.title: Turning Photos into Videos
videos.description:
## Lesson 11 — Turning Photos into Videos

### Why This Matters

Video is the core format on Instagram. Reels typically perform better than static images, and brands are also willing to pay more for video content than photos.

This makes photo-to-video generation an important skill for both audience growth and monetization.

### How to Create a Video from a Photo

Start by uploading your image and describing a **small, natural movement** in the prompt.

Examples include:

* smiling softly
* blinking naturally
* taking a sip of coffee
* hair moving gently

You can also add phrases such as **“natural motion”** to make the result feel more realistic.

A short video of around **8 seconds** is usually enough for reels and social content.

### Important Rule

Keep the movement **small and simple**.

Subtle actions usually produce the best results. Large or complex movements, such as walking, turning, or dramatic body motion, can distort the face and reduce quality.

It is normal to generate **2–3 versions** before selecting the best one.

### Common Mistake

Requesting movements that are too complex. This often causes the face or body to warp and makes the final video look unnatural.

### Today’s Task

Take your **3 best photos** and convert them into short videos using **small, natural movements**.

Generate multiple versions if needed, and save the strongest results.

videos.title: Creating Lip-Sync Videos
videos.description:
## Lesson 12 — Creating Lip-Sync Videos

### The Two-Step Process

Creating a talking AI influencer involves two simple steps:

1. **Write the script** — Decide exactly what your character will say.
2. **Generate the video in Flow** — Upload the image and make the character speak using the script.

A useful prompt structure is:

**“She looks at the camera and speaks naturally, saying: [your dialogue].”**

### Keep the Script Short

For better lip-sync accuracy:

* Keep each video around **8–10 seconds**
* Use approximately **15–20 words**
* Focus on **one clear message per video**
* Use simple, natural dialogue rather than long sentences

Shorter scripts are easier for the AI to sync accurately with mouth movement.

### Improve Pronunciation

If a Hindi or Hinglish word is pronounced incorrectly, write it the way it sounds.

For example:

**“zindagi” → “zindagee”**

Phonetic spelling can help improve pronunciation in generated speech.

### What to Expect

Lip-sync is one of the more difficult AI video tasks, so the first result may not be perfect.

It is normal to generate **3–4 versions** before selecting the strongest one.

### Common Mistake

Using a long sentence or full paragraph in a single video.

This can cause the mouth movement to fall out of sync or the dialogue to get cut off.

### Today’s Task

Write a short **15–20 word introduction** for your AI influencer.

Generate a lip-sync video using the script, create a few variations if needed, and save the best result.

videos.description:
## Lesson 13 — Creating a Consistent AI Voice

### Why Voice Consistency Matters

Just like your character’s face, the **voice should remain consistent across every video**.

A recognizable voice makes your AI influencer feel more natural, professional, and believable.

### The 3 Elements of a Voice

Define your character’s voice using three simple elements:

1. **Pitch** — Soft, medium, or deep
2. **Pace** — Slow, medium, or fast
3. **Tone** — Friendly, calm, confident, energetic, etc.

For example:

**“Soft female voice, medium pace, warm and friendly tone.”**

### Create a Voice Reference

Once you finalize the voice description, use the **exact same wording in every speaking-video prompt**.

Think of it as a **voice reference line**, just like your reference photo is used to maintain facial consistency.

Keep the description simple and specific. Avoid vague phrases such as **“melodious voice”** or **“honey-sweet voice,”** as they may lead to inconsistent results.

### Pro Tip

If the generated voice sounds too artificial, you can mute it during editing and replace it with:

* Your own recorded voice, or
* A suitable AI-generated voice, such as an ElevenLabs Hindi voice

This gives you greater control over the final audio quality.

### Common Mistake

Changing the voice description in every prompt.

Even small changes in pitch, tone, or pace can make your character sound different from one video to another.

### Today’s Task

Finalize your character’s **voice description**, save it in your notes, and use the exact same line to create one new talking video.

videos.title: Reel Editing Basics in VN
videos.description:
## Lesson 14 — Reel Editing Basics in VN

### Keep Editing Simple

You only need four basic editing skills in VN to create a clean, professional reel.

### The 4 Essential Steps

1. **Set the Ratio to 9:16**
   Use the vertical 9:16 format so the video fills the entire mobile screen.

2. **Trim and Arrange Clips**
   Remove unnecessary pauses and cut the first half-second if nothing is happening.
   Starting directly with movement or dialogue helps improve viewer attention.

3. **Add Captions**
   Add text that matches what your character is saying.
   Keep captions clear and readable, such as **white text with a black outline**.

4. **Add Background Music**
   Keep music at around **20–30% volume** so the dialogue remains the main focus.

### Export Settings

Export the final reel in **1080p** for a clean, high-quality result.

### Keep It Professional

Avoid unnecessary transitions, zoom effects, filters, and animations.

Simple editing usually looks cleaner and keeps the viewer focused on the content.

### Common Mistake

Over-editing the reel with too many effects or transitions.

This can make the video feel cluttered and less professional.

### Today’s Task

Create your **first complete reel** using all four steps:

**9:16 ratio → clean cuts → captions → background music**

Then export the final version in **1080p**.

*Editing Lesson — no generation prompt is required.*

videos.description:
## Lesson 15 — Five Reel Formats

### Build a Repeatable Content System

Instead of creating a completely new idea every time, use proven reel formats that can be repeated with different topics, outfits, products, and settings.

### The 5 Reel Formats

1. **GRWM — Get Ready With Me**
   Show your character getting ready or transforming from one look to another.

2. **Day in the Life**
   Create a short sequence showing different moments from your influencer’s day.

3. **Tips**
   Share useful information, such as **3 quick tips** related to your niche.

4. **Trends**
   Use relevant trending formats or audio to make your content feel current and discoverable.

5. **Product Content**
   Feature a product naturally through demonstrations, recommendations, or lifestyle content. This format is especially useful for brand work.

### Rotate Your Formats

Not every format will perform equally well every time.

Instead of relying on one style, rotate your content. A simple approach is:

**3 reels per week → 3 different formats**

After publishing consistently, review which formats receive the strongest response and create more content around those patterns.

### Common Mistake

Using the same format repeatedly or waiting for every reel to perform exceptionally well.

Strong content growth comes from **consistency, testing, and improvement over time**.

### Today’s Task

Choose **2 of the 5 formats** and create **one reel for each**.

Use what you have learned so far about character consistency, video generation, and editing to make both reels complete and ready to publish.

videos.description:
## Lesson 16 — Professional Profile Setup

### Why Your Profile Matters

When someone discovers your reel, they often visit your profile before deciding whether to follow you.

Brands also review your profile before considering collaborations, so your account should look clear, credible, and professional from the beginning.

### The 4 Essentials

1. **Username**
   Keep it short, memorable, and connected to your character’s name or niche.
   Avoid unnecessary numbers and excessive underscores.

2. **Profile Photo**
   Use a clear **close-up image of your character’s face**.
   Avoid full-body photos, as they are difficult to recognize in a small profile icon.

3. **Bio**
   Keep it concise and structured in three lines:

   * Who you are
   * Where you are from
   * A short hook or personality line

   Use only **1–2 relevant emojis** to keep the profile clean.

4. **Professional / Creator Account**
   Switch to a Creator or Professional account to access useful analytics, including:

   * Reel performance
   * Audience activity
   * Engagement insights

### Common Mistake

Uploading too many posts immediately after creating a new account.

Instead, build the profile gradually and focus on quality, consistency, and a professional first impression.

### Today’s Task

Complete your profile setup with:

**Username → Profile Photo → Bio → Creator Account**

Then publish **one strong first post** that represents the style of content you plan to create.

## Lesson 17 — Posting Schedule, Captions & Hashtags

### Build a Consistent Posting Routine

Consistency matters more than posting randomly.

A simple schedule is:

**3 reels per week → 3 different formats**

Choose fixed days and times, such as **Monday, Wednesday, and Friday**, and use your account analytics to identify when your audience is most active.

### Caption Formula

A strong caption should follow a simple structure:

1. **Hook** — Use the first line to grab attention.
2. **Value or Story** — Add 1–2 short lines that explain, inform, or connect.
3. **Call to Action** — Encourage viewers to comment, save, share, or follow.

Your caption should support the reel, not feel like an afterthought.

### Hashtag Strategy

Use around **10–15 relevant hashtags** with a mix of:

* Broad hashtags
* Medium-sized hashtags
* Smaller niche-specific hashtags

Create **2–3 hashtag sets** and rotate them instead of using the exact same group every time.

### Common Mistake

Using generic captions such as **“Nice day”** or adding hashtags without any strategy.

Your caption is an important part of the post and should help communicate the message clearly.

### Today’s Task

Create:

* A **weekly posting schedule**
* **3 reusable caption templates**
* **3 hashtag sets**

Save them in your notes so your future posting process becomes faster and more consistent.

videos.title: Understanding the Reels Algorithm How the Algorithm Thinks
videos.description:
## Lesson 18 — Understanding the Reels Algorithm

### How the Algorithm Thinks

The algorithm is not working against you. Its goal is simple: **keep people engaged on the platform for longer**.

If your reel holds attention and encourages interaction, it is more likely to be shown to a wider audience.

### How a Reel Gains Reach

A reel is usually tested with a smaller group first.

If viewers respond well, the platform gradually shows it to more people.

The stronger the response, the further the reel can travel.

### The 3 Most Important Signals

1. **Watch Time**
   The first second matters the most. Your reel should begin with something that immediately grabs attention.

2. **Completion & Re-Watch**
   Reels that people watch until the end—or watch again—send a strong positive signal.
   Creating a smooth loop can encourage repeat views.

3. **Shares & Saves**
   Content that people save or share is especially valuable because it shows that the reel is useful or worth revisiting.

### The First Hour Matters

Post when your audience is active and respond to comments quickly after publishing.

Early engagement can help your reel build momentum.

### Common Mistake

Starting with a slow or uninteresting first second.

If viewers scroll away immediately, the reel loses its chance to build strong watch time.

### Today’s Task

Review your best-performing reel and study its **first 2 seconds**.

Identify what made people stop and watch, then use a similar opening pattern in your next reel.

For learning, review your own best-performing reel. Inspect the first two seconds, the pacing, the moment

## Lesson 19 — Growing from 0 to 1,000 Followers

### Why 1,000 Followers Matters

Reaching your first **1,000 followers** is an important milestone because it gives your account a stronger base for growth and makes your profile more credible to potential brand partners.

Smaller creators can also be attractive to brands because they often have more focused audiences and stronger engagement.

### A Simple Growth Roadmap

Do not treat 1,000 followers as one large target.

Break it into a consistent system:

**3 reels per week × 8 weeks = 24 reels**

Use different reel formats, stay consistent, and allow time to see which content performs best.

Your first followers may also come from your existing network, which can help build early momentum.

### Engagement Matters More Than Numbers

Followers alone are not enough.

A healthy account is one where people actively:

* Like
* Comment
* Reply
* Share
* Interact with stories

Strong engagement shows that your audience is genuinely interested in your content.

### Daily 20-Minute Engagement Routine

1. **Reply to Comments**
   Respond to comments, especially soon after posting.

2. **Post Stories**
   Use polls, questions, behind-the-scenes content, or simple updates to stay connected with your audience.

3. **Engage With Your Niche**
   Leave **10–15 genuine comments** on relevant posts from other creators or accounts in your niche.

The goal is to participate in the community, not to spam.

### Common Mistake

Publishing content and then disappearing.

Social media is a two-way platform. Accounts grow faster when creators consistently interact with their audience and community.

### Today’s Task

Create an **8-week reel plan** based on three reels per week.

Then complete your first **20-minute engagement routine** today.

## Lesson 20 — Product Photography Basics

### Why Product Photography Matters

Every online seller needs strong product visuals—whether they sell through **Amazon, Flipkart, Instagram, Shopify, or their own website**.

Traditional product shoots can be expensive and time-consuming. AI makes it possible to create professional-looking product visuals much faster and at a lower cost.

### Two Types of Product Photos

There are two main formats:

1. **Clean Product Shot** — Product shown clearly against a simple background.
2. **Lifestyle Shot** — Product shown naturally in a real-world setting.

In this lesson, we focus on the **clean product shot**, which is the foundation.

### How to Create It

Upload both:

* Your AI influencer reference image
* The product image

Then generate a scene where the same character is holding or presenting the product against a clean, simple background.

A useful direction is:

**“Use the same character holding this exact product on a clean, simple background.”**

### Keep the Product Accurate

The product must remain as close to the original as possible.

Check carefully that the AI does not change:

* Shape
* Colour
* Packaging
* Label or branding

### Important Rule

**The product is the hero, not the character.**

Keep the product large, clearly visible, well-lit, and positioned prominently in the frame.

### Common Mistake

Sending an AI-generated image without checking whether the product’s shape, label, or packaging has changed.

Even small inaccuracies can make the final image unsuitable for a client.

### Today’s Task

Choose one simple product, such as a **cup, bottle, or jar**, and create one clean product image with your AI influencer.

Make sure the product remains accurate and clearly visible.

## Lesson 21 — Creating Professional Studio Product Shots

### What Makes a Product Shot Look Professional?

The difference between an average product image and a premium studio shot usually comes down to three elements:

1. **Lighting**
   Use soft studio lighting that clearly shows the product without harsh shadows.

2. **Background**
   Choose a clean white, grey, or neutral background.
   Add a **soft natural shadow beneath the product** so it feels grounded rather than floating.

3. **Camera Angle**
   Choose an angle that best presents the product:

   * **Bottles & Jars** — Eye-level or slightly angled
   * **Jewellery & Watches** — Close-up or slightly top-down
   * **Shoes** — Side or three-quarter view

### Create Multiple Variations

Do not rely on a single image.

Create **2–3 variations or angles** for each product so the client has options and the final set feels more professional.

A strong catalog set might include:

**Front View → Angled View → Detail Close-Up**

### Common Mistake

Using flat lighting with no natural shadow.

This can make the product appear artificial, floating, or poorly integrated with the background.

### Today’s Task

Choose one product and create a **studio-quality catalog set** using:

**Soft lighting + clean background + natural shadow + 3 different angles**

Save the strongest three images as your final product set.

## Lesson 22 — Lifestyle and Platform-Ready Product Shots

### What Is a Lifestyle Product Shot?

A lifestyle product shot places the product in a natural, real-world setting.

For example:

* A **watch worn on the wrist in a café**
* A **candle lit in a cozy room**

This approach helps the product feel more relatable and desirable, because people often connect with the **experience and emotion** around a product—not just the product itself.

That is why lifestyle visuals are often more valuable for brands.

### Create Platform-Ready Images

Different platforms require different types of product images.

* **Amazon / Flipkart Main Image**
  Use a **plain white background**, keep the product large and clear, and avoid adding extra text or distracting elements.

* **Instagram / Website**
  Use **lifestyle visuals** with clean **square or vertical crops**, depending on the platform and content format.

### Why This Matters

Delivering the correct size and crop makes your work more professional.

If the client does not need to crop or adjust the image again, your delivery becomes more useful and client-ready.

### Common Mistake

Using the same image for every platform.

Always ask where the image will be used before creating or delivering it.

### Today’s Task

Create **one lifestyle product image** and **one Amazon-ready white-background image** for the same product.

Save both together as a complete product set.

## Lesson 23 — Fashion Try-On

### Why Fashion Try-On Matters

Fashion products usually perform better when shown on a model rather than as a flat product image.

This makes virtual try-on especially valuable for boutiques, clothing brands, and accessory sellers, as it helps customers visualize the product more clearly and can improve buying confidence.

### How Fashion Try-On Works

Start with:

* Your AI character
* A flat image of the outfit or accessory

Then generate a result where the **same character is wearing the exact product**.

A useful instruction is:

**“Use the same character wearing this exact outfit.”**

### Keep the Product Accurate

The most important rule is that the **print, colour, and design must remain unchanged**.

This is where AI often makes mistakes, so always check the final result carefully before saving or delivering it.

### Create Multiple Looks

You can use this method for:

* Kurtis
* Sarees
* Dresses
* Jewellery
* Accessories

For each product, create **2–3 useful variations**, such as:

* **Full-body view**
* **Half-body view**
* **Close-up detail shot**

This gives the final set more professional value and helps present the product more effectively.

### Common Mistake

Allowing the AI to change the print, pattern, or colour of the original item.

Even small mismatches can make the output unusable for real product presentation.

### Today’s Task

Choose **one outfit or accessory image** and create a try-on result using your AI character.

Then generate **2 additional variations** to present the item in different views.

## Lesson 24 — Getting Your First Client

### Think Like a Problem Solver

You are not simply trying to sell a service.

You are offering a solution to a real business problem: helping sellers improve their product presentation with professional-looking visuals at a more accessible cost.

### Where to Find Potential Clients

Start with small businesses that already need better content, such as:

* Clothing boutiques
* Skincare brands
* Jewellery sellers
* Candle businesses
* Food brands
* Local shops and small online sellers

Instagram is one of the easiest places to find these businesses, especially accounts with good products but weak or inconsistent visuals.

### Use a Simple 3-Line Outreach Message

Keep your message short and personal.

A strong structure is:

1. Mention something specific you genuinely like about their product or brand.
2. Explain briefly that you create professional product visuals for businesses.
3. End with a simple offer, such as:
   **“Would you like me to create a free sample for one of your products?”**

A relevant sample can often communicate your value better than a long sales message.

### Outreach Is a Numbers Game

Not every business will respond, and that is normal.

The goal is to stay consistent:

**5–10 personalized messages per day + polite follow-ups**

Focus on relevant businesses rather than sending the same generic message to everyone.

### Common Mistake

Using copy-paste outreach that feels impersonal, or giving up after receiving one rejection or no response.

Successful outreach requires **personalization, consistency, and follow-up**.

### Today’s Task

Find **10 potential sellers**.

Choose **2 of them**, create one sample visual for each, and send a short personalized 3-line message.

*Strategy Lesson — use the product photography techniques from Lessons 20–23.*

videos.description:
## Lesson 25 — Pricing Your Product Shoots

### Price With Confidence

Pricing is one of the most important parts of working with clients.

Two common mistakes are:

* Charging too much before you have the experience or portfolio to support it
* Charging too little and reducing the perceived value of your work

A better approach is to offer clear packages.

### Create 3 Pricing Tiers

* **Basic** — A few photos, 1 product, 1 platform
  **Starting range: ₹100–₹1,000**

* **Standard** — More photos, multiple angles, and 2 platform formats
  **Starting range: ₹1,000–₹3,000**

* **Premium** — Complete set with studio + lifestyle images and platform-ready formats
  **Starting range: ₹3,000–₹7,000**

These are starting ranges and can increase as your portfolio, quality, and client experience improve.

### Important Pricing Rules

* Do not immediately reduce your price.
  If the client has a smaller budget, **reduce the scope instead**.

* Take an **advance payment** before starting the project.
  A simple structure is: **50% upfront and 50% on delivery**.

* Explain what is included in the package clearly and confidently.

* Once you have shared the price and value, avoid over-explaining or negotiating against yourself.

### Common Mistake

Giving a large discount as soon as the client asks for a lower price.

Instead, offer fewer photos, fewer variations, or a smaller package while maintaining the value of your work.

### Today’s Task

Create a simple **3-tier rate card** with:

**Package Name → What’s Included → Price**

Keep it ready so you can send it immediately when a potential client asks for your rates.

*Strategy Lesson — no generation prompt is required.*

videos.title: Understanding UGC & Creating Your First UGC Video
videos.description:
## Lesson 26 — Understanding UGC & Creating Your First UGC Video

### What Is UGC?

**UGC stands for User Generated Content.**

It is content designed to feel natural and authentic, as if a real customer created it rather than a brand.

This style works because people often trust relatable recommendations more than traditional advertisements.

One major advantage of UGC is that you do not need a large following. Brands can use the content on their own social media pages, websites, or advertising campaigns.

### The Script Is the Most Important Part

A strong UGC video starts with a strong script.

Use this simple 3-part structure:

1. **Hook** — Capture attention in the first few seconds with a problem, question, or bold statement.
2. **Value / Demo** — Explain what the product does and show how it is used.
3. **Call to Action** — End with a clear next step, such as **“Check the link in bio.”**

Keep the complete video short and focused, usually around **20–40 seconds**.

### How to Create the Video

Combine the skills you have already learned:

* Create a lip-sync video with the product visible
* Break the message into **3 short clips**
* Edit the clips in VN
* Use a **9:16 vertical format**
* Keep cuts tight and remove unnecessary pauses
* Add clear captions for every important line
* Use soft background music without overpowering the voice

### Focus on the First 3 Seconds

The opening of the video determines whether viewers continue watching.

Spend extra time improving the **hook**, because a weak opening can reduce the impact of the entire video.

### Common Mistake

Starting with a slow, generic, or uninteresting introduction.

Get to the problem or main benefit immediately.

### Today’s Task

Choose **one product**, write a complete **3-part UGC script**, and create one finished UGC video from script to final edit.

## Lesson 27 — Building Your UGC Portfolio

### Why Your Portfolio Matters

Your portfolio is your **resume, proof of skill, and first impression** in one place.

Brands may spend only a few minutes reviewing your work before deciding whether to contact you, so your portfolio should be clear, focused, and consistently high quality.

### What to Include

Build a portfolio with **5 strong videos** that show variety:

* **2 Testimonial Videos** — Natural, trust-based product recommendations
* **2 Product Demo Videos** — Show how the product works or how it is used
* **1 Different Niche Video** — Demonstrate that you can work across different product categories

Quality matters more than quantity.

**5 strong videos are better than 10 average ones.**

### Where to Host Your Portfolio

Keep everything accessible through **one simple link**.

You can use:

* Google Drive folder
* Simple portfolio page
* Instagram Highlight

At the top, include your name and a clear positioning line such as:

**“UGC Creator — Product Videos Designed to Convert.”**

### Create a Simple Portfolio Presentation

You can also use a Canva **mood board or portfolio template** to present your best clips and images.

Include:

* Your best work
* Your creator name or handle
* A simple title such as **“My Portfolio”**
* Clean, minimal branding

Export it as a **PDF or PNG** if needed.

### Common Mistake

Waiting for your first client before creating a portfolio.

The correct approach is the opposite: **build your portfolio first using sample projects**, then use it to attract clients.

### Today’s Task

Plan your **5 portfolio videos**:

**2 Testimonials + 2 Product Demos + 1 Different Niche**

Organize them in one folder or portfolio page and create a single shareable link.

## Lesson 28 — Reaching Out to Brands

### Target the Right Brands

When you are starting out, focus on **small and medium-sized brands** rather than large companies that usually work through established agencies.

Good categories include:

* Skincare
* Fashion
* Gadgets
* Food
* Lifestyle products
* Small online brands

These businesses often need fresh content and are more accessible to new UGC creators.

### 3 Ways to Reach Brands

1. **Instagram DM**
   Look for brands that are active on Instagram but could improve their product content.

2. **Email**
   Check the brand’s website for contact, marketing, or collaboration details.

3. **Creator & Collaboration Platforms**
   Look for opportunities where brands actively post that they are searching for creators.

### Use a Simple Outreach Formula

Keep your message short, personal, and focused on the brand.

Use this structure:

1. Mention something specific you genuinely like about the product or brand.
2. Briefly introduce yourself as a **UGC creator**.
3. Share your **portfolio link** and offer to create a small sample.

A relevant sample can make your outreach much stronger because the brand can immediately see how your content could work for them.

### Build a Consistent Outreach Routine

A simple daily target is:

**5 Instagram DMs + 2 Emails**

Not every brand will respond, and that is normal.

If there is no reply, send a polite follow-up after **3–4 days**.

### Common Mistake

Sending the same copy-paste message to every brand or spending too much time chasing only large companies.

Personalized outreach to relevant smaller brands is usually a better starting strategy.

### Today’s Task

Create a list of **15 small or medium-sized brands**.

Then:

* Send **5 personalized DMs**
* Send **2 outreach emails**
* Create **1 sample video** for a strong potential brand

## Lesson 29 — Closing the Deal

### Build a Clear UGC Rate Card

Instead of selling only one video, present your service in simple packages:

* **Basic** — 1 video + 1 revision
* **Standard** — 2–3 videos with different hooks
* **Premium** — A complete video set adapted for multiple platforms

A beginner UGC video may be priced around **₹3,000–₹15,000**, depending on quality, scope, usage, and brand requirements.

### Handle Negotiation Professionally

If the client says the price is too high, do not immediately reduce your rate.

**Reduce the scope instead.**

For example:

* Fewer videos
* Fewer variations
* Fewer revisions

If the brand asks for free work, offer only a **small sample**, not a complete campaign.

### Clarify Usage Rights

Always ask where and how long the brand plans to use the content.

Usage matters because content used in paid advertising or for longer periods may justify a higher fee.

### Payment Terms

Use a clear payment structure:

**50% advance before starting + 50% on final delivery**

Keep the agreement in writing, even if it is through email or chat.

### Confirm These 3 Things Before Starting

Make sure both sides clearly agree on:

1. **Number of videos**
2. **Number of revisions**
3. **Usage rights**

Clear expectations prevent confusion and unnecessary extra work later.

### Common Mistake

Agreeing to the project before confirming scope, revisions, payment, and usage.

This often leads to disputes or additional unpaid work.

### Today’s Task

Create your own **UGC rate card** and prepare short responses for these common client questions:

* “Can you reduce the price?”
* “Can you make a free sample?”
* “How long can we use the video?”

*Strategy Lesson — no generation prompt is required.*

## Lesson 30 — Working With Brands & Building Repeat Business

### Why Repeat Clients Matter

Finding a new client can take dozens of messages and multiple follow-ups.

Getting another project from an existing client is much easier.

That is why long-term relationships and repeat work are more valuable than constantly searching for new clients.

### 3 Rules for Professional Delivery

1. **Deliver on Time — or Earlier**
   Meeting deadlines builds trust. Early delivery creates an even stronger impression.

2. **Add a Little Extra Value**
   Include something small beyond what was promised, such as an extra angle, bonus clip, or alternate version.

3. **Keep Files Organized**
   Deliver everything in the correct size, format, and naming structure inside a clean folder.

The easier you make the client’s job, the more professional your service feels.

### Handle Revisions Properly

Complete the number of revisions agreed upon in the deal.

Be open to reasonable feedback, but avoid offering unlimited free revisions.

Clear revision limits protect both your time and the client relationship.

### Turn One Project Into a Monthly Retainer

After a successful delivery, ask whether the brand needs regular content.

A simple message can be:

**“If you need more content, I’d be happy to help. I also offer monthly content packages.”**

This can turn a one-time project into a **monthly retainer** with:

**Fixed content + fixed monthly payment**

Retainers can create more predictable and stable income.

### Common Mistake

Finishing the project and disappearing.

After every delivery, ask for feedback, maintain the relationship, and offer the next project or a monthly package.

### Today’s Task

Create:

* A **delivery checklist**
* A short **repeat-work message**
* A simple **monthly retainer offer**

*Strategy Lesson — no generation prompt is required.*

## Lesson 31 — Affiliate Marketing

### What Is Affiliate Marketing?

Affiliate marketing allows you to earn a commission by recommending products through a special tracking link.

When someone purchases through your link, you receive a percentage of the sale—without managing inventory, shipping, or customer delivery.

Platforms such as **Amazon, Flipkart, and Myntra** offer affiliate programs that creators can join.

### Why It Works Well With an AI Influencer

Your AI influencer is already creating product-based content.

Affiliate marketing simply adds a monetization layer to that content.

A useful reel can continue generating clicks and potential commissions long after it is published.

### How to Get Started

1. **Join an Affiliate Program**
   Start with a platform that matches your audience and content niche.

2. **Choose Relevant Products**
   Focus on products that naturally fit your niche, such as:

   * Fashion
   * Skincare
   * Gadgets
   * Lifestyle products

3. **Create Value-Based Content**
   Instead of directly pushing products, create useful content around them.

   Example:
   **“5 Monsoon Fashion Essentials”**

4. **Share Your Affiliate Links**
   Add them where your audience can easily find them, such as your bio, stories, or other supported link placements.

### Build Trust First

Only recommend products that genuinely fit your content and audience.

Too many random affiliate links can make your profile feel overly promotional and reduce trust.

A better principle is:

**Fewer recommendations + stronger relevance + higher trust**

### Common Mistake

Promoting too many unrelated products simply because they offer commissions.

Trust is more valuable than short-term clicks.

### Today’s Task

Join **one affiliate program**, choose **3 relevant products**, and plan **one value-driven video** that naturally features them.

## Lesson 32 — Creating Your Own Digital Product

### What Is a Digital Product?

A digital product is something you create once and can sell repeatedly without managing inventory, shipping, or physical delivery.

Examples include:

* PDF guides
* Checklists
* Template packs
* Prompt collections
* Content calendars
* UGC script templates

Unlike affiliate marketing, you own both the **product and the revenue from each sale**.

### What Should You Create?

Start with something based on a skill you already understand.

For example:

* AI Influencer Guide
* AI Prompt Pack
* Social Media Content Calendar
* UGC Script Templates

The best digital products solve **one clear problem** for your audience.

Keep your first product simple, focused, and easy to use.

### How to Create and Sell It

You do not need a complex setup.

Create the product using a simple format such as a **PDF or Notion page** with:

* A clean cover
* Clear sections
* Practical steps
* Useful examples or templates

Strong value matters more than complicated design.

To sell it, use a simple payment or checkout link and promote it through content that follows:

**Problem → Solution → Product**

Start with an accessible price, collect feedback and reviews, and improve the product over time.

### Common Mistake

Spending too much time trying to make the product perfect before launching it.

A better approach is:

**Create → Launch → Collect Feedback → Improve**

### Today’s Task

Choose **one digital product idea**, create a simple outline of what it will include, and plan **one reel** that introduces the problem and positions your product as the solution.

## Lesson 33 — Building a Faceless Business Model

### What Is a Faceless Business Model?

Many businesses need regular social media content, but the owner may not have the time, confidence, or interest to appear on camera.

An AI character can become a **consistent digital face for the brand**, allowing the business to create regular content without depending on the owner or a physical model.

### How the Model Works

Choose one business and create a consistent AI character that represents the brand.

This character can regularly appear in:

* Product content
* Offers and promotions
* Educational tips
* Reels and social posts
* Seasonal campaigns

Using the same recognizable character helps the brand build a stronger visual identity and gives customers a familiar face to associate with the business.

### Two Ways to Use This Model

1. **For Your Own Business**
   Use the AI character to create regular content without appearing on camera yourself.

2. **As a Service for Other Businesses**
   Create and manage an AI brand face for clients along with their monthly content.

This can be offered as a **monthly retainer**, where the client receives a fixed amount of content for a fixed monthly fee.

### Why Small Businesses Are a Good Starting Point

Do not focus only on large brands.

Small and local businesses often have a greater need for affordable, consistent content because they may not have dedicated creators, models, or marketing teams.

### Common Mistake

Assuming this service is only useful for large companies.

In reality, **small businesses can be some of the best potential clients** for a simple and reliable AI content system.

### Today’s Task

Choose one business and plan:

* Its AI brand character
* The type of content the character will create
* A simple monthly content package
* One short pitch explaining the service

The goal is to turn your AI content skills into a repeatable business service.

videos.description:
## Lesson 34 — Scaling With Multiple AI Influencers

### What Does Scaling Mean?

Once one AI influencer is working well, you can expand by creating additional characters for different niches such as:

* Fashion
* Technology
* Fitness
* Travel
* Lifestyle

Each character can have its own audience, content strategy, brand opportunities, and income streams.

This allows one person to manage a system that operates more like a small content agency.

### When Should You Create a Second Influencer?

Do not build multiple characters too early.

First, make sure your original influencer has a stable system for:

* Character consistency
* Content creation
* Posting
* Client work
* Monetization

Once that process is working smoothly, you can repeat it with another character.

### Choose a New Niche Carefully

Select a niche with clear demand and monetization opportunities.

Each influencer should have a focused identity and niche rather than trying to cover everything.

For example:

**Fashion Character → Tech Character → Fitness Character**

### Scale With Systems, Not More Effort

Use the same workflow for every character:

**Character Sheet → Content Bank → Reel Formats → Posting Schedule → Monetization**

Once you have a repeatable template, creating the next influencer becomes much faster.

Batch your work as well:

* One day for photos
* One day for videos
* One day for editing and scheduling

This helps you manage multiple characters efficiently.

### Common Mistake

Launching 3–4 influencers at the same time before mastering the first one.

This usually reduces quality across all of them.

A better rule is:

**Build one strong character → create a reliable system → then scale.**

### Today’s Task

If your first AI influencer is already running smoothly, create a plan for your **second character**, including niche, name, style, and content direction.

If not, document your current workflow first so it can later be reused as a scalable system.

courses.description:
AI Filmmaking: From Imagination to Screen
Go beyond generating videos. Learn to tell stories that connect.
Turn your creative ideas into cinematic visuals with Skillomate’s AI Filmmaking course. Designed for beginners, this practical course introduces you to storytelling and AI-powered filmmaking—without requiring previous filmmaking experience, a physical camera, or live actors. 
Across eight focused lessons, learn to shape an idea into a compelling story, build character-reference sheets, and turn your creative direction into shot-by-shot prompts. Use ChatGPT to develop your narrative and plan your visuals, then bring those plans to life in Google Flow. Practise generating takes, selecting stronger results, and connecting shots while maintaining character and scene continuity
Discover how to give every shot a purpose. Explore eight camera-movement approaches and six framing techniques, learning how to use them to build tension, reveal a setting, highlight emotion, or draw viewers into a character’s perspective. The focus is not simply on how a shot looks, but on what it communicates. 
Follow a clear filmmaking framework—Story → Characters → Shots → Sound → Editing—and understand where voiceover and editing fit into the process, with introductions to ElevenLabs and CapCut. Practical exercises and ready-to-use prompts support your learning as you build a foundation in story development, character creation, and cinematic shot generation.

Designed for beginners, this lesson gives you a clear understanding of what the course covers and where to begin. Your first task is to imagine a film idea and choose a direction, such as an emotional story, comedy, or action.

1. Story. This is where you decide the film's idea and emotion. You should know what the film is about and
what its emotional focus will be for the audience. The next lesson breaks this story down into Hook, Build,
Twist and End.
2. Characters. This stage develops the characters who appear in the story. Later, the course teaches you
to create a character description and a character sheet. This stage connects the story's character to a
visual reference that is used in shot generation.
3. Shots. The story is shown on screen through visual shots. Later lessons cover shot prompts, Google
Flow generation, connecting shots, camera movement and framing. The focus at this stage is to turn the
story into individual visuals.
4. Sound. This is the stage for the film's sound. The course's tools include ElevenLabs for voiceovers. The
supplied Lessons 1-8 outline does not explain a detailed sound workflow; for now, remember this stage's
role and position in the sequence.
5. Editing. This is the final stage of the workflow, for which the course uses CapCut. The film material
created earlier is edited here. Detailed editing instructions are not included in the supplied outline.
Key point: return to the map when you are confused
For a story question, think of the Story stage; for a character-reference question, think of the Characters
stage; for a video-generation question, think of the Shots stage. Instead of treating every problem as an
issue with the entire filmmaking process, identify the relevant stage.
Demonstration and practice example
According to the outline, a completed movie is shown in this lesson. Identify the five stages as you watch
it. The supplied file does not include a scene breakdown of that movie. For practice, place the old
voice-note idea on the same map: the story, the young man's character, his shots, the sound and the final
edit.
Today's task
Write a one-line idea for your film and decide its main emotion. Then write the five-step workflow on
your page and place your idea under the Story stage.
Self-check: What is the order of the five steps? Can you describe your film's idea and emotion in one line each?

videos.title: Idea, Emotion + Structure
videos.description:
Build the foundation of your film by choosing an idea with a clear emotional direction. This lesson introduces a four-part storytelling structure: Hook, Build, Twist, and End. You will learn how to capture attention within the first five seconds, develop tension or emotion, introduce an unexpected turn, and finish with an emotionally meaningful ending.
Working with ChatGPT, you will generate ten story ideas, select your preferred concept, and develop it into these four sections. The focus is on turning a broad idea into a structured story rather than moving straight into video generation. Your task is to choose one story and prepare its four-part outline as the foundation for the next stage.
videos.notes:
skillomate
AI FILMMAKING  /  ENGLISH STUDENT NOTES
English translation of the supplied Lesson 04 notesLESSON 04  |  1
LESSON 04 / 08
Idea, Emotion + Structure
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to choose a story idea and divide it into four parts: Hook,
Build, Twist and End. Each part moves the story forward.
Turn an idea into an emotional story
This lesson emphasises emotion. Selecting an idea is not enough; you need to organise the story so that its
emotion and progression are clear. The source connects emotion with virality. The practical focus here is
to develop emotion and structure, not to guarantee reach or views.
Hook: the first 5 seconds. The opening needs to capture the audience's attention. The source highlights
the first 5 seconds. Identify your story's opening separately: what will the audience see first, and what will
interest them in that moment?
Build: increase tension or emotion. After the opening, the story's emotional or tense elements develop.
Connect the Build to the Hook so that the story feels like a connected progression. This part's main role is
to increase emotion, not to jump straight to the ending.
Twist: an unexpected moment. According to the source, the Twist surprises the audience. Identify the
point where something unexpected happens. Continue with your selected idea when writing the Twist so
that all four parts feel like the same story.
End: touch the audience's heart. The final part gives the story an emotional conclusion. The source
focuses on an ending that touches the heart. Write your ending moment separately and consider how it
connects to the emotion you chose at the beginning.
Practical workflow in ChatGPT
First, ask ChatGPT for 10 story ideas. Choose your favourite. Then ask it to divide that selected story into
Hook, Build, Twist and End. The sequence matters: first explore options, then select one idea, and finally
structure that selected idea.
Practice example
Hook: A young man finds a saved voice note from his father. Build: He listens to it sadly. Twist: After a
serious opening, he hears his father's laughter and a funny joke. End: A faint smile appears through his
tears. This is an added practice example, not a breakdown of the movie demonstrated in the source.
Today's task
Choose your favourite from the 10 ideas and ask ChatGPT to create its four-part structure. In your notes,
write what happens in each part. Read all four parts together to check that they continue the same
selected story.
Self-check: What is your Hook? What develops during the Build? Which moment is unexpected, and what is the
emotional End?

Lesson 4 — ChatGPT Prompts (Story)
1) Story ideas nikalne ka prompt
I WANNA DO FILM MAKING WITH AI I WANT A GOOD STORY FILLED WITH EMOTIONS GIVE ME SOME STORY IDEAS A REALISTIC ONE give me 10 STORY IDEAS
2) Chosen story ko structure me todne ka prompt
Perfect 1ST ONE Take this story and break it into a 4-part short film structure — HOOK (first 5 seconds), BUILD (rising tension), TWIST (surprise), and END (emotional punch). Keep it realistic and emotional.

videos.title: Generation Prompt + Character Sheet
videos.description:
Turn your story into the prompts and visual references needed for video generation. Continuing in the same ChatGPT conversation, you will create a character description and a character reference sheet prompt. This sheet presents the same face from multiple angles and with different expressions, giving you a visual reference for your film.
Next, you will prepare up to six shot prompts, repeating the same character and location details in each prompt to support consistency. The lesson keeps the project focused on a short, manageable film. You will then use the character sheet prompt in Google Flow, review the generated results, and select the reference you want to use when creating your shots.
videos.notes:
skillomate
AI FILMMAKING  /  ENGLISH STUDENT NOTES
English translation of the supplied Lesson 05 notesLESSON 05  |  1
LESSON 05 / 08
Generation Prompt +
Character Sheet
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to create a character-reference sheet and a maximum of six
shot prompts for your selected story, then choose the best character reference in Google Flow.
Continue in the same ChatGPT chat
Use the same ChatGPT chat in which you developed the story and its four-part structure to create the
character description and shot prompts. The lesson's order is clear: first the CHARACTER SHEET prompt,
then a maximum of six shot prompts. Every prompt should continue the same selected story.
What should a character sheet contain?
A character sheet is a reference image showing the same face from different angles and with different
expressions. Its purpose is to prepare a reference for one character, not a collection of different
characters. The main check is whether the same face appears in every angle and expression.
This differs from a single, ordinary portrait: the source specifically asks for a reference with multiple angles
and expressions. Consider the character description and reference sheet together; this reference will be
used later for shot generation.
Shot prompts: a maximum of 6
Ask ChatGPT for a maximum of six shot prompts. Repeat the same character description and the same
location in every shot. Describing the character only in the first shot and leaving it out of the others does
not follow this lesson's instruction. Each shot's written description should maintain the required
consistency.
The source clearly instructs you to keep the film short. Instead of increasing the shot count unnecessarily,
prepare a limited set of prompts for the selected story. This lesson's output is a manageable character
reference and a short set of shot prompts.
Duration note: The source states exactly "1-2 min (~70-85 sec)". It does not provide a detailed breakdown of per-shot durations,
clip limits or total running time.
Lock in your reference in Google Flow
Generate the character sheet in Google Flow using its prompt, then select and lock in the best reference.
Here, "lock" means continuing to use that selected reference; the supplied outline does not name a
specific identity-lock button.
Practice example
One possible practice example is a sheet showing the same young man from the front and side, with
neutral and sad expressions. These illustrate angles and expressions; they are not a mandatory list from
the source.
Today's task
Ask ChatGPT to create a character-sheet prompt and six shot prompts. Check that every shot repeats the
same character and location. Then generate the character sheet in Flow and select your best reference.
Self-check: Does the sheet show the same face throughout? Does every shot repeat the character and location? Are
there no more than six shot prompts?
videos.examplePrompt:
Lesson 5 — ChatGPT Prompt (Generation + Character Sheet)
Act as an AI film director. Here is my 4-part structure for a SHORT film "[STORY NAME]". I want a 1–2 minute film, so keep it to MAXIMUM 6 shots total — do NOT expand it into many scenes.
Give me the output in this exact order:
PART 1 — CHARACTER SHEET PROMPT: write ONE image-generation prompt that creates a CHARACTER REFERENCE SHEET — the SAME face shown in multiple angles in one image (front view, 3/4 view, side profile) plus a row of expressions (neutral, sad, crying). Include age, face, hair, skin, and exact clothes. This is a reference sheet, NOT a single normal photo.
PART 2 — SHOT PROMPTS (max 6): ready-to-use Google Flow (Veo) video prompts, shot by shot. RULES: repeat the SAME character description AND the SAME location in EVERY shot so face and place stay consistent. Each shot: camera angle, camera movement, lighting, and the action. Realistic, cinematic, vertical 9:16. No on-screen text, no watermark, NO background music.
Keep it emotional, realistic, and SHORT.
Film shot (character — from chat G.P.T, then Flow)
[character full description], [action], [location], [camera angle + movement], [lighting]. Realistic, cinematic, vertical 9:16, real skin, natural hands with five fingers, no on-screen text, no watermark, NO background music.
Face-consistency (Ingredients mode — Lesson 6 trick)
USE THIS IMAGE [saved last frame] AS THE FIRST FRAME AND TO KEEP THE FACE CONSISTENT THIS IS THE CHARACTER SHEET [character reference sheet]. [character description]. [location]. [shot action]. Realistic, cinematic, 9:16, no on-screen text, no watermark, NO background music.

videos.title: Generate the First Shot + Connect Shots
videos.description:
Begin bringing your film to life by generating shots in Google Flow. This lesson covers the reference-to-video process: attaching your character reference, entering the shot prompt, and generating a clip. You will also learn to compare two or three generated takes and select the strongest result.
The lesson then introduces a technique for connecting clips: saving the last frame of one shot and using it as the starting frame for the next. You will also explore how Ingredients mode combines the previous frame and character reference sheet with text instructions to address facial inconsistencies. Your practice task is to generate several shots using these methods, focusing on character consistency and continuity between clips.
videos.notes:
skillomate
AI FILMMAKING  /  ENGLISH STUDENT NOTES
English translation of the supplied Lesson 06 notesLESSON 06  |  1
LESSON 06 / 08
Generate the First Shot +
Connect Shots
By the end of this lesson, you will understand how to generate the first shot from a character
reference, choose the best take and use its last frame as the starting frame for the next shot.
From reference to video
You will now use the character reference and shot prompts from Lesson 5 in Google Flow. This lesson
focuses on creating individual shots and connecting them. The character reference, generated clip and
that clip's last frame are separate assets; it is important to understand the role of each in the process.
Generate the first shot
The supplied workflow is: go to Reference-to-video, attach the character reference, paste the shot prompt
and generate. Use the same character reference that you selected in the previous lesson. For the prompt,
use the relevant shot from your prepared shot-prompt set.
The source instructs you to generate two or three times and choose the best take. Select from the
generated versions of the same shot. The output of this step is the selected clip that you will use next. The
source does not specify an exact quality score or an automated selection method.
The trick for connecting shots
First, SAVE the last frame of your selected clip. Use this saved image as the Start frame for the next clip,
then generate the next shot. In this sequence, the previous clip's ending frame becomes the starting
reference for the next clip; this connection is the lesson's focus.
Remember the order: selected clip, save its last frame, use it as the next clip's start frame, then generate
again. During practice, check that you saved the last frame from the correct selected clip. Do not treat the
character sheet and last frame as interchangeable: one is the character reference, while the other is the
previous shot's ending visual.
Face-fix: Ingredients mode
The source's face-fix method is to provide two images in Ingredients mode: the previous shot's last frame
and the original character sheet. Add text explaining what you need. The images have different roles: the
last frame relates to shot continuity, while the character sheet provides a reference for the same
character.
Tool note: Reference-to-video, Start frame and Ingredients are labels from the supplied outline. The source does not provide
exact current interface steps or the complete wording of the face-fix instruction.
Practice example
Generate a shot for the old voice-note idea. Select the best clip, save its last frame and use it as the start
frame for the next shot. This practice applies the source's shot-connection workflow.
Today's task
Generate a few shots using this process for practice. Make sure you can identify your reference, selected
clips and saved last frames so that you use the correct asset for the next generation.
Self-check: How does a last frame differ from a character sheet? Which two images does the source require for the
Ingredients face-fix method?
